name: Represent a tenth as a decimal
description: Student can represent one tenth in decimal form.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown one part of a bar split into 10, the student writes 0.1.
commonError: Student writes 1.0 or 0.10 for one tenth, confusing the place.
checkpointTask: Show tenths on bars or number lines. Ask the student to write each as a decimal.

name: Represent a hundredth as a decimal
description: Student can represent one hundredth in decimal form.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown one part of a hundred grid, the student writes 0.01.
commonError: Student writes 0.1 for one hundredth, ignoring the hundredths place.
checkpointTask: Show hundredths on a grid. Ask the student to write each as a decimal.

name: Read a decimal number
description: Student can read a decimal number to hundredths.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown 3.07, the student reads 'three and seven hundredths'.
commonError: Student reads 3.07 as 'three point seven', dropping the place.
checkpointTask: Show decimals to hundredths. Ask the student to read each correctly.

name: Show a decimal with materials
description: Student can represent a decimal using a place value model or grid.
exampleOfSuccess: For 1.4, the student shows one whole and 4 tenths.
commonError: Student shows the digits as whole numbers, ignoring the decimal point.
checkpointTask: Name decimals to tenths and hundredths. Ask the student to model each.

name: Recognise tenths and hundredths relationships
description: Student can recognise that one is ten tenths and one tenth is ten hundredths.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 1 is the same as 10 tenths, and 0.1 is the same as 0.10.
commonError: Student thinks 0.1 and 0.10 are different sizes.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to explain how tenths, hundredths and ones relate.

name: Identify odd and even numbers
description: Student can identify odd and even numbers by their last digit.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 46 is even because it ends in 6, and 23 is odd.
commonError: Student judges by the whole number rather than the last digit.
checkpointTask: Name numbers. Ask the student whether each is odd or even and how they know.

name: Explain why a number is even
description: Student can explain that an even number can be shared into two equal groups with none left over.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 8 is even because it makes two equal groups of 4.
commonError: Student states odd or even with no reasoning.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to explain why a number is even using sharing.

name: Predict odd and even results
description: Student can predict whether the result of adding or multiplying will be odd or even.
exampleOfSuccess: The student predicts odd plus odd is even.
commonError: Student guesses without using the property.
checkpointTask: Pose sums and products. Ask the student to predict odd or even before calculating.

name: Use odd and even to check
description: Student can use odd and even properties to check a calculation is sensible.
exampleOfSuccess: The student notices an even plus even giving an odd answer must be wrong.
commonError: Student does not use parity to spot an error.
checkpointTask: Give calculations with some parity errors. Ask the student to spot the impossible ones.

name: Find an equivalent fraction
description: Student can find an equivalent fraction using related denominators.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 1/2 is the same as 2/4.
commonError: Student changes only the numerator or only the denominator.
checkpointTask: Give fractions. Ask the student for an equivalent one and to justify it.

name: Show equivalence with a model
description: Student can use a model such as folded paper or a fraction wall to show two fractions are equivalent.
exampleOfSuccess: Folding paper, the student shows 2/4 covers the same as 1/2.
commonError: Student lines up unequal parts and calls them equivalent.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to show that two fractions are equivalent using a model.

name: Connect a fraction to a decimal
description: Student can connect a fraction to its decimal form for tenths.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 3/10 is the same as 0.3.
commonError: Student writes 3/10 as 3.10 or 0.10.
checkpointTask: Give fractions in tenths. Ask the student to write each as a decimal.

name: Connect common fractions to decimals
description: Student can connect common fractions such as 1/2 and 1/4 to their decimal forms.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 1/2 is 0.5 and 1/4 is 0.25.
commonError: Student writes 1/2 as 0.2 or 1/4 as 0.4.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to write 1/2, 1/4 and 3/4 as decimals.

name: Count by fractions
description: Student can count forwards and backwards by a fraction.
exampleOfSuccess: The student counts 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 5/4.
commonError: Student counts the numerators as whole numbers, losing the fraction.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to count by quarters and by tenths.

name: Locate a fraction on a number line
description: Student can locate and represent a fraction on a number line.
exampleOfSuccess: The student marks 3/4 between 0 and 1, splitting the line into quarters.
commonError: Student places fractions by guess without equal intervals.
checkpointTask: Give a number line. Ask the student to mark several fractions.

name: Locate a mixed numeral on a number line
description: Student can locate a mixed numeral on a number line.
exampleOfSuccess: The student marks 1 and 1/2 halfway between 1 and 2.
commonError: Student places the mixed numeral as if it were less than 1.
checkpointTask: Give a 0 to 3 number line. Ask the student to mark mixed numerals.

name: Convert between mixed and improper fractions
description: Student can convert a mixed numeral to an improper fraction and back.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes 1 and 3/4 as 7/4.
commonError: Student adds the whole number to the numerator without using the denominator.
checkpointTask: Give mixed numerals and improper fractions. Ask the student to convert each.

name: Multiply by 10 and 100
description: Student can multiply a natural number by 10 and 100 using place value.
exampleOfSuccess: For 24 x 10, the student gives 240, explaining the digits shift one place.
commonError: Student just adds a zero without understanding the place value shift.
checkpointTask: Pose multiplications by 10 and 100. Ask the student to solve and explain.

name: Divide by 10 and 100
description: Student can divide a number by 10 and 100 using place value.
exampleOfSuccess: For 600 divided by 10, the student gives 60.
commonError: Student removes a zero mechanically and errs when there is no trailing zero.
checkpointTask: Pose divisions by 10 and 100. Ask the student to solve and explain.

name: Multiply by multiples of 10
description: Student can multiply by a multiple of 10 using known facts.
exampleOfSuccess: For 6 x 30, the student uses 6 x 3 = 18 then x 10 to get 180.
commonError: Student multiplies by the digit only, ignoring the multiple of 10.
checkpointTask: Pose multiplications by multiples of 10. Ask the student to solve.

name: Solve a problem using powers of 10
description: Student can solve a practical problem involving multiplying or dividing by powers of 10.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'how many 10 cent coins make $4', the student finds 40.
commonError: Student chooses the wrong operation or place value shift.
checkpointTask: Pose problems involving powers of 10. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Use an efficient addition strategy
description: Student can choose and use an efficient strategy to add larger numbers.
exampleOfSuccess: For 348 + 199, the student adds 200 and subtracts 1.
commonError: Student always uses the standard algorithm even when a smarter strategy fits.
checkpointTask: Pose additions suited to mental strategies. Ask the student to solve efficiently.

name: Use doubling and halving for multiplication
description: Student can use doubling and halving to multiply efficiently.
exampleOfSuccess: For 4 x 25, the student halves and doubles to make 2 x 50 = 100.
commonError: Student doubles one number without halving the other.
checkpointTask: Pose multiplications suited to doubling and halving. Ask the student to solve.

name: Use an array or area model to multiply
description: Student can use an array or area model to multiply two numbers.
exampleOfSuccess: For 6 x 14, the student splits into 6 x 10 and 6 x 4 to get 84.
commonError: Student multiplies only part of the number, forgetting the tens or ones.
checkpointTask: Pose two-digit multiplications. Ask the student to solve using an area model.

name: Solve a division with no remainder
description: Student can solve a division problem that divides evenly.
exampleOfSuccess: For 96 divided by 4, the student finds 24.
commonError: Student leaves a remainder where the numbers divide evenly, or divides only part.
checkpointTask: Pose divisions that work out evenly. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Round a number to estimate
description: Student can round numbers to make an estimate.
exampleOfSuccess: For 487, the student rounds to 500.
commonError: Student rounds to the wrong place, or rounds down when it should round up.
checkpointTask: Give numbers and a place to round to. Ask the student to round each.

name: Estimate a calculation
description: Student can estimate the result of a calculation using rounding.
exampleOfSuccess: For 312 + 489, the student estimates about 800.
commonError: Student rounds inconsistently, or rounds after calculating.
checkpointTask: Pose calculations. Ask the student to estimate the result before solving.

name: Check a calculation is reasonable
description: Student can use an estimate to judge whether an answer is reasonable.
exampleOfSuccess: Getting 801 for 312 + 489, the student checks it against the estimate of 800.
commonError: Student accepts an unreasonable answer without checking.
checkpointTask: Give answered calculations. Ask the student to estimate and judge each.

name: Estimate a financial total
description: Student can estimate the total cost of several items.
exampleOfSuccess: Estimating a shop, the student rounds prices and adds to about $20.
commonError: Student adds exact prices slowly or rounds wrongly.
checkpointTask: Give a short shopping list. Ask the student to estimate the total.

name: Choose the operation and strategy
description: Student can choose the operation and an efficient strategy for a practical problem.
exampleOfSuccess: For a sharing problem, the student chooses division and a known fact.
commonError: Student picks an operation by the numbers rather than the situation.
checkpointTask: Pose practical problems. Ask the student which operation and strategy each needs.

name: Model an additive problem
description: Student can model and solve a practical additive problem, writing a number sentence.
exampleOfSuccess: For a two-step problem, the student writes and solves the number sentences.
commonError: Student solves only one step of a multi-step problem.
checkpointTask: Pose additive problems. Ask the student to model, write a number sentence and solve.

name: Model a multiplicative problem
description: Student can model and solve a practical multiplication or division problem.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'seats in 8 rows of 6', the student finds 48.
commonError: Student adds instead of multiplying.
checkpointTask: Pose multiplicative problems. Ask the student to model and solve each.

name: Model a money problem with a budget
description: Student can model a practical money problem such as a simple budget.
exampleOfSuccess: For a party budget, the student adds the costs and checks against the money available.
commonError: Student leaves out a cost or does not compare to the budget.
checkpointTask: Pose a budgeting problem. Ask the student to model and solve it.

name: Interpret the solution in context
description: Student can interpret and communicate the solution in terms of the situation.
exampleOfSuccess: After finding $18, the student says 'that is under our $20 budget, so we can afford it'.
commonError: Student gives a number without relating it to the problem.
checkpointTask: After a problem, ask the student what the answer means for the situation.

name: Follow an algorithm using operations
description: Student can follow an algorithm that uses addition or multiplication to generate numbers.
exampleOfSuccess: Following 'start at 3, add 4 each time', the student generates 3, 7, 11, 15.
commonError: Student applies the rule inconsistently or changes the step.
checkpointTask: Give a number-generating algorithm. Ask the student to follow it.

name: Create an algorithm for a sequence
description: Student can create an algorithm that generates a number sequence.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes steps to generate multiples of 6.
commonError: Student writes steps that are unclear or generate the wrong sequence.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to write an algorithm to generate a given number pattern.

name: Represent an algorithm as a flow chart
description: Student can represent an algorithm as a simple flow chart.
exampleOfSuccess: The student draws a flow chart with a start, a repeated step and an output.
commonError: Student draws steps with no clear order or missing the loop.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to draw a flow chart for a number-generating algorithm.

name: Describe the emerging pattern
description: Student can describe the pattern that emerges from running an algorithm.
exampleOfSuccess: After generating multiples of 6, the student says they all are even and increase by 6.
commonError: Student lists the numbers without describing the pattern.
checkpointTask: After running an algorithm, ask the student to describe the pattern.
